items.hook: Things women were told were ugly for absolutely no reason
items.subtitle: A short list. A very daft one.
items.text1: Freckles. Laughter lines. A big nose. A natural curl. Hips. Hair with a mind of its own. All of it, at some point, was apparently a problem.
items.text2: It was never a problem. It was a person with a face. It is time we stopped taking advice from a magazine from 1996.
items.cta: What were you told was ugly that you now love? Tell me.

items.hook: Things Gen X women were never taught about skin
items.subtitle: We were left to work it out alone.
items.text1: Nobody said wear SPF every day. Nobody said you can leave the sunbed. Nobody said a good cleanser is a friend.
items.text2: We learned it the hard way and we are passing it on with love. Our daughters will roll their eyes. That is how you know it works.
items.cta: What do you wish someone had told you about skin at 18? Pass it on.

items.hook: Things we put on our faces in the 90s and somehow survived
items.subtitle: And somehow we lived to tell the tale.
items.text1: Baby oil, lemon juice, toothpaste, Sun-In, a pink shimmer and a thick line of kohl. Often all at once, on a Saturday.
items.text2: Our faces are tougher than any of us knew. I salute you, my fellow survivors. I hope you are using SPF these days.
items.cta: What is the worst thing you put on your face in the 90s? Share the shame.

items.hook: Things our mothers did to their faces that would get TikTok removed
items.subtitle: With love and a bit of a gasp.
items.text1: Cold cream on everything. A flannel in boiling water. A bit of Vaseline. A very firm slap in the name of circulation.
items.text2: They did their best with what they had and they looked great. Let us have a laugh and a lot of admiration.
items.cta: What did your mum do to her face that you remember? Tell me.

items.hook: Things menopause has stolen and frankly needs to return
items.subtitle: I would like it all back. Please.
items.text1: My sleep. My patience. My ability to find a word. A very good memory for names and the whole concept of a cool bedroom.
items.text2: We will manage, with humour and a good fan. But a note to menopause: this is a robbery and we know who you are.
items.cta: What would you like returned first? Sleep, memory or a good temperature?

items.hook: Things I wish TikTok would stop teaching women
items.subtitle: I am begging you. Put the phone down.
items.text1: A cure for everything in a kitchen cupboard. A shortcut to perfect skin. A trick that costs nothing and promises everything.
items.text2: Some of it is fun. Some of it is nonsense. All of it is delivered by a person with a ring light and a lot of energy.
items.cta: What is the daftest tip you have seen online? Share it. I will give it a mark.

items.hook: Things I would ban if I became aesthetics dictator for 24 hours
items.subtitle: A very short and very firm rule book.
items.text1: Magnifying mirrors. Filters that remove pores. Comparing yourself to someone who is paid to look shiny. Overhead lighting in changing rooms.
items.text2: In their place there would be soft lamps, kind words and a cup of tea at every counter. A fair and gentle regime.
items.cta: What would you ban? Write your rule and I will pass it to the committee.

items.hook: Things I'd tell you if the consultation room had no CCTV
items.subtitle: Ssh. Do not tell anyone.
items.text1: I would say you are lovely, you are doing fine and the thing you are worried about is invisible to everyone else.
items.text2: I would also say be careful with the internet and its advice, and be kind to the face in the mirror. It has done a lot.
items.cta: What would you like to be told, with no cameras? I am listening.

items.hook: Things your practitioner discusses in the car afterwards
items.subtitle: A very honest debrief, probably.
items.text1: I imagine it goes something like this: what a lovely lot of people today, where did we put the lunch and who needs a message.
items.text2: Mostly kindness, a bit of planning and a lot of crisps. It is the best part of the day, whoever is driving.
items.cta: What do you chat about in the car after an appointment? Tell me.

items.hook: Things that make practitioners stare into the middle distance
items.subtitle: A look. You know the look.
items.text1: A request for a face from a film. A request to 'take a bit off, but not change it'. A question about something that happened in 2003.
items.text2: I breathe in, take a moment and find the kindest way to answer. It is a skill. Possibly a superpower.
items.cta: What is the most surprising thing you have asked a professional?

items.hook: Things patients show me on Instagram that make my eye twitch
items.subtitle: A tic that comes and goes.
items.text1: A photo with seven filters and a lot of edits. A face that no human has. A request to look just like that on a Monday.
items.text2: It makes me smile and then it makes me sigh. Real faces are the best ones. They move, they crease and they laugh.
items.cta: What is the most unrealistic thing you have seen on a screen? Tell me.

items.hook: Things I could say in clinic but enjoy being employed
items.subtitle: Left unsaid. For job reasons.
items.text1: Many things. Some about lighting. Some about the internet. Some about a husband who thinks everything is fine, which is lovely, if slightly beside the point.
items.text2: I will keep my opinions on the polite side of the line and save the rest for a friend and a very good biscuit.
items.cta: What is something you would say if there were no consequences? Spill.

items.hook: Things I'd rather do than recreate your favourite influencer's face
items.subtitle: A list in order of preference.
items.text1: Wash the car with a toothbrush. Alphabetise the spices. Sit through a family quiz about Latin. All easier than copying someone else's face.
items.text2: Your face is the only one in the world with your smile. Let us talk about how to make it the best version of itself.
items.cta: What would you rather do than copy someone else? Mine is the spice rack.

items.hook: Things men secretly ask me about
items.subtitle: More of them than you would think.
items.text1: 'Is it vain to ask?' 'Do people notice?' 'What is a good moisturiser?' Often in a low voice and with a quick look at the door.
items.text2: Everyone has the same questions. Everyone deserves a kind answer. Looking after yourself is a very good idea.
items.cta: Do you know a man who would love some skin advice? Tag him and be kind.

items.hook: Things I judge as a practitioner
items.subtitle: I am not proud. I am only human.
items.text1: I judge how a person is with a receptionist. I judge a person who says they have no time for sleep. I judge a coat on the floor.
items.text2: I judge nothing about your skin. That is the one bit I am here to help with, kindly and with a lot of curiosity.
items.cta: What do you judge other people for? Fess up. It makes you human.

items.hook: Things I am refusing to turn into a problem: smile lines, looking 48 at 48 and a face that moves.
items.subtitle: Add your own. I am keeping a list.
items.text1: A smile line is a place a lot of smiling has been. Looking 48 at 48 is accurate. A face that moves means you have something to say.
items.text2: All of it is a person living. I will keep celebrating it for as long as someone is selling the opposite.
items.cta: What are you refusing to turn into a problem? Add yours to the list.

items.hook: Things I'd fix before your face: your sleep, your algorithm, your magnifying mirror and your belief that 47 should resemble 27.
items.subtitle: In this order, please.
items.text1: Sleep first. Then the 'for you' page that makes you feel small. Then the magnifying mirror in the bathroom. Then a gentle chat about a plan.
items.text2: And a reminder that a very well rested 47 is a lovely thing to be. Aim for your own face on a really good day.
items.cta: What would you fix before your face? Say it plainly.

items.hook: Things I could sell you today but won't
items.subtitle: A shortlist, with a smile.
items.text1: A lot of things. A product you do not need. A package you will not use. A promise I cannot keep. A bargain with a deadline.
items.text2: I would rather you leave with a plan that fits, a clear idea of what to do and a good feeling about it.
items.cta: What is the best bit of advice you got that saved you money?

items.hook: Things that happen after 40: the stairs have opinions, your knees have a voice and your skin has a diary.
items.subtitle: I have more. Many more.
items.text1: Your ears get sharper about the wrong noises and duller about the right ones. You say 'in my day' and mean it, with love.
items.text2: A lot of it is funny and a few bits are a little tender. All of it is better with friends and a laugh.
items.cta: What happened to you after 40 that you did not expect? Add to the list.

items.hook: Things that belong in 2016
items.subtitle: A pause for the ones that went with it.
items.text1: Contouring with a spade. Thick brows drawn on with a marker. A choker. Skinny jeans so tight we could not breathe. All of it, loved.
items.text2: Trends come and go and the good bits stay. Let us say goodbye with affection and no regret. Maybe a little regret.
items.cta: What trend would you like to leave in 2016? And which one do you secretly miss?

items.hook: I have seen things in this clinic that would make a nun blush.
items.subtitle: Mostly handbags, honestly.
items.text1: The most shocking thing about anyone's life is how much we all carry. Bags, worries, lists. A whole picnic, sometimes, for no reason.
items.text2: I find it endearing. We are all slightly overpacked and trying our best. It is why I love people and their handbags.
items.cta: What is the strangest thing in your handbag right now? I will not tell.

items.hook: BREAKING: Local woman discovers she has pores. Investigation ongoing.
items.subtitle: Experts are on the scene.
items.text1: Sources say they have been there since birth. Scientists are shocked. Local residents are calm and say they were always going to turn up.
items.text2: Our reporter advises you not to zoom in. Nothing good has ever come of it. Please remain seated and put the mirror down.
items.cta: What did you discover on your face this week? Share it with the newsroom.

items.hook: BREAKING: 47-year-old woman looks 47. Family said to be coping well.
items.subtitle: Family said to be coping well.
items.text1: Neighbours confirm she looks exactly 47. A source close to her says she looks wonderful and has just ordered a very comfortable cardigan.
items.text2: She is said to be thriving, laughing loudly and refusing to apologise for it. Residents are encouraged to follow her lead.
items.cta: How old are you and how are you coping? Give us a statement.

items.hook: BREAKING: Forehead moves when woman raises eyebrows. Experts baffled.
items.subtitle: Experts are baffled and a bit delighted.
items.text1: A forehead has been seen moving in response to an eyebrow. Specialists say this is called expression and it has been a human feature for a very long time.
items.text2: The woman in question says she has a lot to express. Reports suggest she is doing it with gusto.
items.cta: What does your forehead do when you are surprised? Show us the face.

items.hook: BREAKING: Gravity continues operating without regulatory approval.
items.subtitle: A spokesperson declined to comment.
items.text1: Gravity has been operating for some time with no sign of stopping. Insiders say it is nothing personal and it affects everything from socks to cheeks.
items.text2: We urge the public to stay calm, wear a supportive bra and carry on. Further updates as they fall in.
items.cta: Where has gravity struck you? Report in the comments.

items.hook: BREAKING: Woman survives seeing herself on accidental front camera.
items.subtitle: She is in a stable condition.
items.text1: A woman opened her phone and found the front camera had been left on. She screamed, then laughed, then had a glass of water.
items.text2: Witnesses say it was a bad angle, a bad light and a bad time. Nothing was wrong with her. The camera was at fault.
items.cta: What is your worst accidental selfie? Describe the angle.

items.hook: BREAKING: Local mum hasn't drunk water since Tuesday. Blames collagen.
items.subtitle: She blames collagen. Collagen has not replied.
items.text1: A local mum has not had a glass of water since Tuesday. She had three coffees, a tea and a very small sip from the dog's bowl.
items.text2: Officials are urging her to drink up. She says she will after the school run, the shopping and the next 42 jobs.
items.cta: How much water have you had today? Be honest. We are not the police.

items.hook: BREAKING: Woman buys seventh serum. First six unavailable for comment.
items.subtitle: The first six are unavailable for comment.
items.text1: A woman has purchased her seventh serum. The first six are at the back of the cabinet, unopened and looking at each other.
items.text2: Experts say a simple routine done every day beats a shelf of hopeful bottles. She says she is aware and has already clicked buy.
items.cta: How many serums are lurking in your cupboard? Say the number.

items.hook: BREAKING: Magnifying mirror arrested following disturbance in bathroom.
items.subtitle: A search of the bathroom is under way.
items.text1: Police were called to a bathroom after a magnifying mirror was found making everyone look surprised. It has been taken in for questioning.
items.text2: A spokesperson said no human face was designed to be seen at ten times its size. The mirror says it was only doing its job.
items.cta: Do you own a magnifying mirror? Admit it. It will not help your case.

items.hook: BREAKING: Instagram filter accused of crimes against normal faces.
items.subtitle: A trial date has been set.
items.text1: A filter has been accused of smoothing, shrinking and swapping faces with no consent. Faces everywhere are said to be relieved by the news.
items.text2: Witnesses say real people have pores, lines and freckles and those are the good bits. The filter is said to be unrepentant.
items.cta: Do you use a filter? What does it change? No judgement, just curiosity.

items.hook: BREAKING: Woman smiles. Lines appear. Nation stunned.
items.subtitle: Nation stunned. Tea consumed.
items.text1: A woman smiled today. Lines appeared around her eyes. Scientists say these are called laughter lines and they are a sign of a life well enjoyed.
items.text2: Residents are asked to remain calm and, where possible, to smile back. It is a very infectious condition.
items.cta: What made you smile today? Break the news.

items.hook: BREAKING: Woman spends £247 on skincare. Still requires sleep.
items.subtitle: Experts say sleep was free.
items.text1: A woman has spent £247 on skincare. Her skin is said to be fine. She is said to be very tired. Neighbours report a lovely smell.
items.text2: A source says an early night and a glass of water would have done the trick. She says she knows. She has already added to basket.
items.cta: What is the most you have spent on skincare? Say the amount. We will hold your hand.

items.hook: BREAKING: Husband says "I can't see anything wrong." Situation escalates.
items.subtitle: The situation is escalating.
items.text1: A husband said he could not see anything wrong. His wife said that was not the question. A tense silence followed, with a tea.
items.text2: Experts say the right answer was 'you look lovely, and what do you need?' The husband is said to be learning.
items.cta: What did your other half say that was meant well but landed badly?

items.hook: BREAKING: Woman turns camera around accidentally. Emergency services notified.
items.subtitle: Emergency services have been notified.
items.text1: A woman turned the camera round by accident. She saw a double chin, a ceiling fan and a cat. She is shaken but fine.
items.text2: Experts advise holding the phone higher and using a window. A lamp is a good friend. A ceiling light is a foe.
items.cta: What is your best selfie tip? Share it with the nation.

items.hook: BREAKING: Clinic confirms nobody needs to look 24 forever.
items.subtitle: A statement was read out calmly.
items.text1: A clinic has confirmed that nobody has to look 24 forever. A big sigh of relief was heard across the nation and a few cheers.
items.text2: The statement went on to say that looking like yourself is the goal and that you can be fabulous at every age.
items.cta: What age did you look your best? Or are you waiting for it?

items.hook: BREAKING: Bathroom lighting charged with malicious wounding.
items.subtitle: The bulb denies everything.
items.text1: Bathroom lighting has been charged with making everyone look tired, grey and slightly haunted. Witnesses say it is always harsh and always overhead.
items.text2: A kind lamp in a kind corner is recommended as a safe alternative. A candle works too. A very low dimmer is best of all.
items.cta: Where is the most flattering light in your house? Tell me the room.

items.hook: BREAKING: Woman, 49, bends down without making noise. Scientists demand further testing.
items.subtitle: Scientists demand further testing.
items.text1: A woman aged 49 bent down to pick up a sock and stood back up without a sound. Neighbours say they have never seen anything like it.
items.text2: A team of experts is on its way. She says it was a good day, a good knee and a good sock.
items.cta: What noise do you make bending down? Do the sound effect.

items.hook: BREAKING: Local woman sleeps eight uninterrupted hours. Neighbours describe her as "unrecognisable".
items.subtitle: Neighbours describe her as unrecognisable.
items.text1: A local woman slept eight uninterrupted hours and woke up looking rested, glowing and a little bit confused. She went to find her phone to prove it.
items.text2: She says it was the best night of her life. Her family has not seen her smile like that since 2011.
items.cta: What is the best night's sleep you ever had? Where were you?

items.hook: BREAKING: Woman drinks two glasses of wine and remains functional next morning. Vatican investigating.
items.subtitle: The Vatican is investigating. Reportedly.
items.text1: A woman drank two glasses of wine and woke up fine, with no headache. She said 'I feel like a new woman' and everyone cheered.
items.text2: Scientists are asking whether it was the wine, the water, the mood or the moon. A full investigation will take place on Saturday.
items.cta: How many glasses of wine does it take to ruin your next day? Tell me your number.

items.hook: BREAKING: 47-year-old opens front camera accidentally. Phone recovered from garden.
items.subtitle: No injuries. A lot of dignity lost.
items.text1: A woman aged 47 opened her phone and met a version of herself she was not expecting. The phone was thrown. It landed in a hedge.
items.text2: Emergency services reported that the phone survived and that the woman is now in a lovely mood. Be careful with the front camera.
items.cta: What is the worst thing the front camera has shown you? Share, in your own time.

items.hook: BREAKING: Husband says "you don't need anything doing". Wife confirms this was not the question.
items.subtitle: Wife confirms this was not the question.
items.text1: A husband said 'you don't need anything doing.' He meant it kindly. The wife heard it and felt a rush of love and a rush of fury.
items.text2: Experts say the best answer to a question like this is 'thank you, you are sweet', followed by a very long hug.
items.cta: What kind thing has someone said that you did not want to hear? Go on.

items.hook: BREAKING: Woman asks partner if he notices anything different. Search party deployed.
items.subtitle: A search party is being prepared.
items.text1: A woman asked her partner if he noticed anything different. He looked at the ceiling, the telly and the cat. He said 'you look nice.'
items.text2: He was not wrong. He was not right. A new hairstyle, a pair of earrings and a very expensive candle were all missed.
items.cta: What did your partner fail to notice? Tell me what it was.

items.hook: BREAKING: Local woman discovers 10x mirror. Funeral Thursday.
items.subtitle: The funeral is on Thursday. Bring a tissue.
items.text1: A local woman discovered a ten times magnifying mirror in a drawer. She picked it up. She looked. She put it down. She sat for a while.
items.text2: Her friends say she is doing well and has taken up a hobby. The mirror has been moved to a very high shelf.
items.cta: Where is your magnifying mirror hiding? Do you use it? Be brave.

items.hook: BREAKING: Menopause denies involvement despite overwhelming evidence.
items.subtitle: Overwhelming evidence has been found.
items.text1: Menopause has denied any involvement in the sleep, the sweats, the mood, the hair and the missing words. Witnesses disagree and have receipts.
items.text2: A woman says she knows what she saw. A fan, a window and a duvet were all involved. The case continues.
items.cta: What did menopause take from you first? Give your evidence.

items.hook: BREAKING: Collagen leaves family home without forwarding address.
items.subtitle: It left no note. Possibly a postcard.
items.text1: Collagen has left the family home without a forwarding address. Friends say it had been talking about a change for a while.
items.text2: A search is under way. Experts suggest sleep, sunscreen, good food and a gentle approach to what is still here.
items.cta: When did you notice the first sign? Tell me what it was.

items.hook: BREAKING: 50-year-old wears bikini without asking internet permission. Nation survives.
items.subtitle: The nation survived. Reports of joy.
items.text1: A 50 year old woman wore a bikini on a beach without asking the internet for permission. The sea did not rise. The sun came out.
items.text2: Witnesses say she had a lovely time, an ice cream and a very good book. Experts say this is how it should be.
items.cta: What would you wear if you did not ask permission? Tell me.

items.hook: AESTHETICS COURT: Instagram charged with making normal women think they look strange.
items.subtitle: The defence is a lot of filters.
items.text1: The prosecution says normal women have been made to feel strange by pictures of people who do not look like that. Even they do not look like that.
items.text2: The jury is made up of everyone who has ever scrolled at midnight. The verdict will be read after tea.
items.cta: How do you vote, guilty or very guilty? Tell me in the comments.

items.hook: AESTHETICS COURT: Defendant admits requesting "natural but snatched".
items.subtitle: The judge asked for a definition.
items.text1: The defendant says she wants to look natural and snatched at the same time. She has been asked to clarify and says 'just very good, but not noticeable'.
items.text2: The court admits it is a lovely idea. The judge asks that all requests be made in a clear, honest and kind way.
items.cta: How would you describe your dream look in three words? Put it in the dock.

items.hook: AESTHETICS COURT: Prosecution asks why defendant owns 11 serums but drinks no water.
items.subtitle: The prosecution rests. The water jug is empty.
items.text1: The defendant owns eleven serums and has not drunk a glass of water since breakfast. The court gasps. A lady in the front row nods.
items.text2: The judge suggests starting with water. The defence says it is a work in progress and has an exciting new product on the way.
items.cta: What goes first, a serum or a day without water? Plead below.

items.hook: AESTHETICS COURT: Magnifying mirror receives 25 years without parole.
items.subtitle: No parole. Not even for good behaviour.
items.text1: The mirror was found guilty of causing alarm, distress and an unscheduled visit to the fridge. It shows no remorse and it is very shiny.
items.text2: The sentence has been carried out with a cloth over its head in a cupboard. The court thanks everyone for their service.
items.cta: What would you sentence it to? Let us pass the sentence together.

items.hook: AESTHETICS COURT: Overhead lighting convicted on all counts.
items.subtitle: A unanimous verdict. Cheers all round.
items.text1: Overhead lighting was found guilty of making every face look tired, every shadow look dramatic and every changing room look like a crime scene.
items.text2: It has been ordered to attend a course on softness. It will be released on a dimmer switch with a warm bulb.
items.cta: Which room has the worst lighting? Name and shame the venue.

items.hook: AESTHETICS COURT: Woman accused of diagnosing herself after watching three Reels.
items.subtitle: She was warned three times.
items.text1: The woman in the dock watched three videos, read two comments and diagnosed herself with a very rare condition. She feels fine, which is suspicious.
items.text2: The judge advises that a short video is not a medical degree and that a good chat with a professional is worth a hundred reels.
items.cta: Have you ever googled something at 2am and panicked? Tell the court.

items.hook: AESTHETICS COURT: Menopause facing 47 separate charges.
items.subtitle: The charge sheet is very long.
items.text1: Charges include stealing sleep, hiding keys, turning up the heat and removing the word 'tomorrow' from a perfectly good memory.
items.text2: Menopause has pleaded not guilty and sent a very hot flush as a message. The court is adjourned for a fan.
items.cta: Add a charge to the sheet. What would you accuse it of?

items.hook: AESTHETICS COURT: Gravity refuses to apologise.
items.subtitle: A statement will not be issued.
items.text1: Gravity has been asked to say sorry for its work on cheeks, eyebrows and certain socks. It said it was only doing what it was told by Newton.
items.text2: The court agreed that gravity is not going anywhere. It recommends a good bra, a sense of humour and a very nice cardigan.
items.cta: What would you ask gravity to apologise for? Read out your statement.

items.hook: AESTHETICS COURT: Ageing found NOT GUILTY. Society ordered to calm down.
items.subtitle: Society has been told to calm down.
items.text1: Ageing was found not guilty of all charges. The judge said it had been doing its job for millions of years and had done it very well.
items.text2: Society was ordered to stop making women feel bad about it. Case dismissed. Tea and cake to be served on the steps.
items.cta: What do you love about getting older? Tell the court.

items.hook: AESTHETICS COURT: SPF found innocent on all counts.
items.subtitle: A very good character witness appeared.
items.text1: SPF was found innocent on all counts. It was accused of being greasy, boring and a bit of a chore. It was none of those things.
items.text2: Witnesses say it has stood by us in the sun, on the school run and in the garden. Everybody has agreed to give it a hug.
items.cta: What SPF do you use every day? Put it in the court record.

items.hook: AESTHETICS COURT: Defendant claims "my friend said it was fine."
items.subtitle: The court has heard this before.
items.text1: The defendant says her friend told her it was fine. The friend is not here today. She was last seen with a strong opinion and a bargain.
items.text2: The judge suggests asking someone qualified and not someone who is merely confident. Court is adjourned for biscuits.
items.cta: What did a friend tell you was fine that was absolutely not fine?

items.hook: AESTHETICS COURT: Woman sues menopause for damages.
items.subtitle: Damages are being calculated.
items.text1: A woman is taking menopause to court over sleep, sweat and a very short fuse. She is asking for damages and a quiet room.
items.text2: Her legal team says she has a strong case and a very small fan in her handbag. The first witness is her thermostat.
items.cta: What would you ask for in damages? Name the amount in biscuits.

items.hook: CLINIC CRIME REPORT: Woman caught examining pores at 14x magnification.
items.subtitle: The suspect refused to put the mirror down.
items.text1: A woman was caught examining her pores at fourteen times magnification. She said she was 'just checking'. Nobody believed her.
items.text2: Officers advise that no human has ever looked at their skin from six inches away and felt great. Please step away from the mirror.
items.cta: How close do you get to your mirror? Be honest. Measure in inches.

items.hook: CLINIC CRIME REPORT: Repeat offender slept in make-up.
items.subtitle: It was not the first offence.
items.text1: A repeat offender was found asleep in last night's mascara, with a pillow case to match. She pleaded tiredness and a very good film.
items.text2: She was let off with a warning and a cleansing wipe. The pillow case was not as lucky and will be sent to the wash.
items.cta: Have you ever slept in your make-up? Tell the court. We will go easy on you.

items.hook: CLINIC CRIME REPORT: SPF found unopened. Suspect claims "I work indoors."
items.subtitle: The bottle is in the bathroom. Still sealed.
items.text1: A bottle of SPF was found unopened in a drawer. The suspect said 'I work indoors.' The window behind her was very large.
items.text2: Officers say daylight comes through glass, through clouds and through excuses. She has been asked to apply daily.
items.cta: What is your SPF excuse? Tell the officer.

items.hook: CLINIC CRIME REPORT: Suspect purchased skincare because bottle was pretty.
items.subtitle: She was seduced by the packaging.
items.text1: A woman bought a skincare product because the bottle was pretty. It had a gold lid and a very elegant font. She did not read a thing on it.
items.text2: Experts say it is a very common crime. The ingredients are inside, the bottle is just the outfit. Check the label next time.
items.cta: What is the prettiest thing you have bought for the bottle alone?

items.hook: CLINIC CRIME REPORT: Woman used daughter's skincare. Daughter seeking damages.
items.subtitle: The daughter is seeking damages.
items.text1: A mother was found using her daughter's skincare while the daughter was at school. She claimed it was 'only a little bit'. It was half a jar.
items.text2: The daughter has noticed. The daughter has a good memory. A small payment in chocolate has been suggested.
items.cta: Have you ever borrowed from a daughter, a sister or a friend? Come clean.

items.hook: CLINIC CRIME REPORT: Face wipe discovered beneath pillow.
items.subtitle: Found at the scene. Still damp.
items.text1: A face wipe was discovered under a pillow. It had been placed there at 1am with a good intention and a very sleepy hand.
items.text2: Police believe the suspect meant to throw it away. Officers advise a bin next to the bed or a very firm word with yourself.
items.cta: What is the weirdest thing you have found in your bed? Report it.

items.hook: CLINIC CRIME REPORT: Woman arrived saying "I've been Googling." Practitioner requests backup.
items.subtitle: Backup was requested. Tea was served.
items.text1: A woman arrived with notes, a printout and a very worried look. She said she had been Googling. A kettle was switched on straight away.
items.text2: Officers say Google knows a lot but it does not know you. A kind, patient chat with a real person can clear up a lot of worry.
items.cta: What have you been Googling lately? Tell us. We will not tell Google.

items.hook: CLINIC CRIME REPORT: Fake tan applied at 11:47pm before 6am flight.
items.subtitle: She looked fabulous. It was dark.
items.text1: A woman applied fake tan at 11.47pm before a 6am flight. She went to bed like a glazed biscuit and woke up looking like a tangerine.
items.text2: Witnesses say she sailed through security looking very sporty. Her white sheets are still being treated as evidence.
items.cta: What is your worst fake tan story? Take us to the scene.

items.hook: CLINIC CRIME REPORT: Seven active ingredients found fighting in one bathroom cabinet.
items.subtitle: Peace talks have broken down.
items.text1: Seven active ingredients were found fighting in one bathroom cabinet. Three acids, two serums and a very confused moisturiser were involved.
items.text2: A neutral party advises a simple routine, introduced slowly, with a gentle hand. Not every product has to attend every meeting.
items.cta: How many products are in your routine? Give a number and a mood.

items.hook: CLINIC CRIME REPORT: Ring light charged with creating unrealistic expectations.
items.subtitle: It denies everything. It is very bright.
items.text1: A ring light was charged with creating unrealistic expectations. It said it just wanted everyone to look glowing and slightly circular.
items.text2: Witnesses say nobody looks like that in real life and that is absolutely fine. The ring light has been unplugged.
items.cta: Do you own a ring light? Does it make you feel glam or alarmed?

items.hook: CLINIC CRIME REPORT: SPF abandoned during 28-degree heatwave.
items.subtitle: The sun was out. So was the suspect.
items.text1: SPF was abandoned during a 28 degree heatwave. The suspect was found under an umbrella with a very red nose and a very large hat.
items.text2: A bottle was nearby with the cap still on. Officers say it works much better if it comes out of the handbag.
items.cta: What is your sunburn story? Tell the officer the shade.

items.hook: Search history of a 47-year-old woman: "Best serum for neck." "Is 9pm too early for bed?" "Hotels Ibiza quiet." "Where did my eyebrows go?"
items.subtitle: Her phone is being treated as evidence.
items.text1: It is a very honest list. A little worry, a lot of curiosity and a firm longing for a quiet holiday and a very good night's sleep.
items.text2: The searches say she is human, tired and funny. They also say she will find that serum, that hotel and that eyebrow, eventually.
items.cta: What is in your search history that you would never say out loud?

items.hook: Google searches we will never admit to: "Why does my face look old only in car mirrors?" "Can menopause move your eyebrows?" "Can you divorce gravity?"
items.subtitle: Clear your history before reading.
items.text1: We all type something odd at midnight. A very specific worry, a strange question or a symptom we diagnose ourselves with.
items.text2: Nobody is judging. Everyone does it. If something is worrying you, ask a real person, over a cuppa, in daylight.
items.cta: What is the strangest thing you have searched? Tell me, I will keep it quiet.

items.hook: Patient: "I want natural." Translation: "If Brenda from accounts notices, somebody has overdone it."
items.subtitle: A very handy phrasebook.
items.text1: Natural means a bit of a lift, a lot of rest and a face that looks like yours on a really good day. Nothing obvious, nothing dramatic.
items.text2: Brenda from accounts is a wise woman. If she does not notice, you have done it right. If she says you look well, take the win.
items.cta: What does natural mean to you? Describe it in three words.

items.hook: Patient: "I just want a consultation." Meaning: "I've researched this for eleven months and already know your dog's name."
items.subtitle: Dog's name included.
items.text1: She has read every article, watched every video and bookmarked a forum from 2014. She is more prepared than most people at their own wedding.
items.text2: That is lovely. Do your research. Come with your list, your questions and your tea. It is always worth the preparation.
items.cta: How many tabs do you have open for something you are thinking about?

items.hook: Your 25-year-old self reviews you: "Wait. We own a business? We stopped caring what men think? And we can afford good skincare?"
items.subtitle: Her feedback is mixed but enthusiastic.
items.text1: She is stunned by the business, the confidence and the sensible shoes. She is thrilled that we stopped caring what a few people think.
items.text2: She is a bit worried about the knees and very excited about the skincare. She says 'well done us.' We say 'thank you, love.'
items.cta: What would your 25 year old self think of you now? Give her a review.

items.hook: Voicemail from your future self: "Hi. It's you at 62. Wear the bloody SPF. Also, dump Gary."
items.subtitle: Please save this message.
items.text1: Hi love. It is you at 62. Things are good. The knees are the same. The laughs are louder. And the sun is lovely, because of the SPF.
items.text2: Also, please stop worrying about things that will not matter. Drink the tea, book the holiday and leave Gary behind.
items.cta: What would your 62 year old self say to you today? Press play.

items.hook: My face's out of office: "Jawline unavailable until further notice. For urgent enquiries contact cheekbones."
items.subtitle: Please try the cheekbones. They are in.
items.text1: My jawline will be away until further notice. It has taken a long holiday and not left a number. A sign on the door says 'back soon, maybe'.
items.text2: In the meantime I am delighted to introduce my cheekbones, my laugh lines and a very nice scarf. They are covering the shift.
items.cta: What is out of office on your face today? Leave a message.

items.hook: Midlife patch notes: "Woman 4.9 update installed: confidence upgraded, patience removed, ability to detect nonsense increased 84%."
items.subtitle: Please restart for the changes to take effect.
items.text1: Version 4.9 is installed. Confidence is upgraded. Patience has been removed. The ability to detect nonsense is up 84 per cent.
items.text2: Known issues include a short temper at 3pm, a longer nap and a fresh opinion on a lot of things. No refunds. All fixes are free tea.
items.cta: What has been upgraded in your latest update? What would you like removed?

items.hook: Face MOT: "Jawline: advisory. Skin: passed. Lips: no work required. Magnifying mirror: immediate failure."
items.subtitle: A full report is on the fridge.
items.text1: The jawline needs a keen eye. The skin has passed with flying colours. The lips are doing a lovely job. The magnifying mirror failed immediately.
items.text2: A few advisories remain: more water, more sleep, less scrolling. Next test due in twelve months, or after a very nice holiday.
items.cta: What would your face MOT say? List your advisories.

items.hook: Ofsted for your skincare: "Retinol: Outstanding. SPF attendance: Requires Improvement. Face wipes: Special Measures."
items.subtitle: Inspectors will return for a follow up visit.
items.text1: Retinol is outstanding, though a bit demanding. SPF attendance requires improvement. Face wipes have been placed in special measures.
items.text2: The cleanser is a good citizen. The moisturiser is showing real progress. The serum collection has been asked to consider its priorities.
items.cta: What grade would your skincare routine get? Give it a mark and a comment.

items.hook: Official statement: a woman may simultaneously love herself and fancy having something done.
items.subtitle: Signed. Dated. Stamped with a heart.
items.text1: It is hereby declared that a woman can love herself and want a little help. These things sit side by side on the sofa.
items.text2: Nobody has to choose between feeling good and wanting a little more. You are allowed both, and a biscuit.
items.cta: Do you agree? Sign below with a heart or a comment.

items.hook: Official guidance: looking tired is not compulsory.
items.subtitle: Issued with immediate effect.
items.text1: It is not compulsory to look tired. It is also not compulsory to look wide awake. You can look like yourself with a decent night and a nice lamp.
items.text2: Anyone who suggests otherwise is welcome to come and discuss it over a hot drink. The kettle is on and the door is open.
items.cta: What do you think counts as 'looking tired'? Give your definition.

items.hook: Policy update: women over 40 no longer required to explain why they want treatment.
items.subtitle: Effective from now. No exceptions.
items.text1: Women over 40 are no longer required to explain why they would like to do something for themselves. A smile and 'because I fancied it' is plenty.
items.text2: A form will not be needed. A reason will not be needed. A cuppa and a chat will be provided to anyone who would like one.
items.cta: What are you no longer explaining? Give the reason or the lack of one.

items.hook: BREAKING: Parliament votes overwhelmingly to abolish magnifying mirrors.
items.subtitle: Applause was heard in all bathrooms.
items.text1: The motion was carried by a very large majority. Magnifying mirrors are to be abolished, replaced with kind lamps and a small mirror on a stick.
items.text2: The nation breathed a sigh of relief. There was a spontaneous round of applause and a lot of people checked their cabinets.
items.cta: How would you vote? Yes, absolutely, or yes, definitely?
